admission.justification: The harness-specific rule was on the table and rejected for a neutral one; the choice binds every future instruction text.

alternatives.option: Write instruction texts without naming a harness, provider or model: 'If your harness offers helpers (sub-agents), they run on your own seat's model unless the developer names another'; a role's harness and model come from its role settings and a harness's quirks go on that harness's documentation page.
alternatives.reason: A rule hard-coded to one harness does not apply to the others, and Claude is not always the Architect's harness.

alternatives.option: Keep the harness-specific rule 'On Claude Code, your own sub-agents run on Opus unless the developer names another model.'
alternatives.reason: It assumes one harness and one model for every seat.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A per-role helper setting exists and a harness needs a rule that its settings cannot express.

consequences: The Pi specifics live in docs/install/pi.md.
A per-role helper setting is a later row; the code is unchanged.
context: A rule picked from the dashboard said 'On Claude Code, your own sub-agents run on Opus unless the developer names another model', and four more l-01 places named one harness or provider. Whether and how a role uses sub-agents is a role setting.
decider: The developer (D709); MIK-R84 v14 behaviour 1, seventh rule.
